constraint_decided_it: Specificity (CRMarchaeo A8 Stratigraphic Unit / A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit, both descendants of E26 via S20 Rigid Physical Feature) versus B's core-CRM E25/E26; plus P37's scope note, 'The same identifier may be assigned on more than one occasion', which contradicts B's rejected-alternative claim that one shared E42 instance would 'overstate the coordination'.
better_modelling: Two stratigraphic units: the Trench 3 posthole cut is more precisely A3 Stratigraphic Interface (A3 covers surfaces 'formed by the removal or destruction of existing stratifications'), the Trench 7 fill is A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit. One E42 Identifier with P190 symbolic content '56' may legitimately be P1-linked to both, since P1 is many to many (0,n:0,n) and P37 allows the same identifier to be assigned on more than one occasion; the collision is carried by two E15 Identifier Assignment events, each P140 assigned attribute to its own unit, P37 assigned '56', P14 carried out by the respective supervisor, P4 has time-span 1978. The two context sheets are instances of E31 Document (P70 documents) and the archive should mint new disambiguating identifiers, attaching them with P48 has preferred identifier (0,1:0,n) while '56' stays a legacy identifier.
reasoning: Both answers reach the same core result (two entities, one identifier-layer collision) and both quote E42's 'within the context of one or more organisations' accurately; A's t0633 quote ('He issued identifiers') and B's crm732 narrative quotes ('the formal instances in a knowledge base are the identifiers, not the real things or phenomena'; 'informed people are able to agree that they refer to the same, single thing...') all verify verbatim, so neither is unsupported. A wins on specificity: the case is explicitly stratigraphic recording, and A applies A8/A2 and correctly rules out A6 Group Declaration Event against its actual scope note (it requires an interpretive claim that the units are remains of one former whole), whereas B stops at the general ancestors E25/E26 and additionally asserts 'purposely created' intentional backfilling that the case never states. B's second rejected alternative is a model-level error: P37's scope note explicitly permits the same identifier to be assigned on more than one occasion, and E42 individuation follows symbolic content, not the assignment act, so 'two E42 instances with coincidentally identical content' is an artifact rather than what the CRM prescribes. A's only defect is leaving the posthole at generic A8 where A3 Stratigraphic Interface applies, and both omit P140 and the E31 context sheets.
